messages.subject: Bifactor Question
parts: I have a question about Bifactors in IRT which is not specific to the package. If you run a bifactor with a majority of items from one scale and then a few items from another scale will that bias the general factor? For example, in the NEO personality scale you have several facets (Anxiety, Hostility, Depression, Self-consciousness, implusiveness, and vulnerability) which when a bifactor is conducted the general factor would be Neuroticism and the facets would be the grouping constructs. However, if you had an abundance of anxiety items (maybe 8 out 12) would the bifactor then just produce the general factor of anxiety and the loading of the other 4 items are just residual loadings which would be smaller than if the general factor was neuroticism? Or would bifactor detect the general factor as being Neuroticism no matter the overabundance of anxiety items?

messages.author: 58786c912f9ee9c2
messages.subject: Re: Bifactor Question
parts:
Hi Gene,

the answer is yes, the main factor will be biased. Another interpretation is, that the main factor is only interpretable relative to an item set and is not an absolute property of an item. I do not have a nice reference for this, but we ran some simulations a while ago and analysed some data from another personality scale (coincidentally also neuroticism).

How large the bias is, will depend on the ratio of the items, their variances and their intercorrelations. The easiest way I found to look into this is to resample items or systematically vary the ratio. The correlation of the main factor with the anxiety items will increase as their number increases. As a consequence I believe scale construction needs to make sure a priori that facets are equally well represented in the item set.

Kind wishes,
Philipp (Doebler)
